headline: This space skips
body: Everything gets framed hormonally, as if the only inputs are molecules you swallow or inject. Bone is a mechanically responsive tissue and that gets left out.
punch: Load is a signal your skeleton reads directly.

headline: The study
body: A controlled intervention in short-stature children, measuring serum growth hormone, IGF-1, IGFBP-3, and the IGF-1 to IGFBP-3 ratio before and after.

headline: The ratio
body: IGFBP-3 binds IGF-1 in circulation. The ratio between them approximates how much IGF-1 is actually free to act, rather than how much simply exists.
punch: Total IGF-1 is not available IGF-1.

headline: Why loading works
body: Bone and cartilage cells respond directly to mechanical strain. Impact loading is a recognised anabolic stimulus for bone independent of any hormone you add.
punch: The tissue has its own input channel.

headline: The design limits
body: Non-randomised, controlled but not blinded, and the endpoints are blood markers — not adult height. Nobody followed these children to final stature.
punch: Moved a marker. Did not demonstrate more height.

headline: Which is the honest frame
body: A hormonal marker moving in a favourable direction is a long way from a centimetre gained. That gap is where most of this niche's confident claims live.

headline: Still worth knowing
body: It's free, it has no adverse-effect profile, and the mechanism is real. Very little else in this topic can claim all three at once.
punch: The floor for this intervention is 'harmless'.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
